subsystems.name: Key switches
subsystems.role: the moving element under each key that registers a press.
parts: membrane dome or scissor mechanism (laptops and cheap boards)
mechanical switch with spring, stem and metal contacts
optical switch using an infrared beam
Hall-effect or inductive switch sensing a magnet

subsystems.name: Keycaps
subsystems.role: the surfaces your fingers touch, labelled with characters.
parts: moulded ABS or PBT plastic cap

subsystems.name: Plate and case
subsystems.role: hold the switches in a rigid grid that stops flex and damps sound.

subsystems.name: Circuit board and matrix
subsystems.role: wires hundreds of keys into a small number of signal lines.

subsystems.name: Controller and firmware
subsystems.role: scans the matrix, debounces signals and reports key events.
parts: firmware (open-source layouts such as QMK or vendor equivalents)

subsystems.name: Interface and power
parts: Bluetooth or 2.4 GHz radio and battery (wireless models)

subsystems.name: Backlighting
subsystems.role: illuminates legends for use in the dark.
parts: per-key LEDs or an edge-lit light guide

buildSteps.title: Design the layout and matrix
buildSteps.detail: Decide the key arrangement, then assign each key a row and column so a modest number of pins can scan them all.

buildSteps.title: Lay out the circuit board
buildSteps.detail: Traces, diode positions and switch footprints are drawn, then boards are etched and assembled with surface-mount diodes and a microcontroller.

buildSteps.title: Make the switches
buildSteps.detail: Contacts, springs and stems are stamped and moulded, then snapped together in clean conditions so grit cannot jam them.

buildSteps.title: Mould the keycaps
buildSteps.detail: Plastic is injected into polished moulds; double-shot moulding or dye sublimation applies legends that will not rub off.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate plate and case
buildSteps.detail: Metal plate is stamped or laser-cut with switch cut-outs; the case is injection-moulded or machined.

buildSteps.title: Assemble
buildSteps.detail: Switches are pressed into the plate and soldered or socketed to the board, which is screwed into the case and topped with keycaps.

buildSteps.title: Flash firmware
buildSteps.detail: Matrix mapping, debounce timing, keymap and lighting behaviour are compiled and loaded.

buildSteps.title: Test
buildSteps.detail: Automated rigs press every key and check for missed or doubled presses; a human types a sample before packing.

prerequisites.why: lets any keyboard report keystrokes to any computer without a custom driver.
each keyboard needs a chip to scan the matrix and speak USB or Bluetooth.
switch housings and keycaps must fit within fractions of a millimetre.
determines feel, lifespan and whether the press is binary or analogue.
the matrix and its diodes live on a custom board, often made in small batches.

pathway.milestone: mechanical and membrane keyboards with per-key lighting and 1000 Hz USB polling
pathway.unlocks: reliable, cheap text input for nearly every computer.

pathway.milestone: magnetic and optical switches with adjustable actuation and rapid-trigger modes
pathway.unlocks: faster, more precise control in games and lower latency typing.

pathway.milestone: analogue key sensing reported to software as continuous values
pathway.unlocks: pressure-sensitive input in games, music and accessibility tools.

pathway.milestone: adaptive key surfaces and haptic feedback instead of fixed rows of keys
pathway.unlocks: layouts that reconfigure for the task, language or user.
